input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard operability fixes for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard-accessibility defects identified by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. On completion,
all four flows are fully operable with keyboard alone — no focus traps, no
unreachable controls — and visible focus indicators are consistent across the
audited flows.

## Scope

- Remediate every defect enumerated in the accessibility audit report for the
  four audited flows, including:
  - Focus loss and focus trapping in modals (focus must be moved into the
    modal on open, contained while open, and restored to the invoking control
    on close).
  - Controls unreachable via keyboard (tab order, roving tabindex, and
    keyboard activation for interactive elements).
  - Inconsistent or invisible focus indicators across the audited surfaces.
- Apply a consistent focus-indicator treatment across the four flows so
  keyboard users can always identify the focused control.
- Keep the fixes scoped to keyboard operability: screen-reader semantics beyond
  what the keyboard fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones, are
  out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the project creation flow, When it is operated end to end with keyboard
  only, Then it completes with no focus traps and no unreachable controls.
- Given the workbench spawn flow, When it is operated end to end with keyboard
  only, Then it completes with no focus traps and no unreachable controls.
- Given the model deployment flow, When it is operated end to end with keyboard
  only, Then it completes with no focus traps and no unreachable controls.
- Given the pipeline run submission flow, When it is operated end to end with
  keyboard only, Then it completes with no focus traps and no unreachable
  controls.
- Every control reachable by pointer in the four audited flows is also
  reachable and activatable by keyboard.
- Visible focus indicators are present and visually consistent across all
  interactive controls in the four audited flows.
- Existing pointer-driven operation of the four flows is not regressed by the
  fixes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls. Covered by this epic's
  remediation of all audit-enumerated defects across the four flows.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows. Covered by this epic's consistent focus-indicator treatment over the
  same four flows.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
to reflect the fixed keyboard-operability state of the four core Dashboard
flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run
submission). It delivers the published VPAT and the product docs accessibility
statement that two public-sector customers require before renewal.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) so the conformance
  claims for the four audited flows reflect the remediated keyboard-operability
  state, including the criteria covered by the keyboard fixes.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the
  current supported keyboard-operability state of the audited flows.
- Republish both artifacts through the Red Hat documentation content process.
- Keep the documentation scoped to the keyboard fixes: conformance claims about
  screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and flows
  outside the four audited ones, are out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT's conformance statements for the four audited flows reflect the
  remediated keyboard-operability state, and every updated claim is accurate
  against the shipped implementation.
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated to describe the current
  keyboard-operability state of the audited flows and republished.
- The updated documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  fixes by the team that delivered them, and review findings are addressed
  before publication.
- The republished VPAT and accessibility statement are publicly available at
  their documented locations.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)** — The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review. Covered by this epic's update,
  technical review, and republication of both artifacts.
